title: Chapter 2 — Send-Forth
description: The last week in Iyana-Wahala: the pap stall at dawn, the Honourable's photographers, and a street that throws you a party you didn't ask for.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Five a.m. The pap stall by the bus stop. Mama stirs; you fry. The first danfo drivers come for akara before their first passenger.

beats.speaker: mamaSomto
beats.text: Last week of frying, my son. After this, you hold books, not ladles. (She laughs.) Fry well, so they remember the scholar's akara.

good.toast: Mama counts the morning's money twice and hides ₦2,000 in your box when she thinks you're not looking.

bad.toast: "You gave the conductor credit again? He will pay in heaven."

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Ten o'clock. Two Hilux trucks. Photographers. Barrister Àjàyí, and a banner: "HON. OWÓ ŃLÁ EMPOWERS IYANA-WAHALA YOUTH". The youth is you.

beats.speaker: settlement
beats.text: Mr. Somtochukwu. Stand here. Hold the scholarship letter like this. The Honourable's hand on your shoulder. Smile like the future.

options.text: Smile wide. Hold the letter high.
Pull Mama into the photo. "She made me. Not the Foundation."
Stand in the photo with a straight face. Say nothing.

beats.speaker: settlement
beats.text: (handing you an envelope) Transport money. The Honourable is generous to the grateful.

variants.text: (very tightly) The Honourable prefers... cleaner photos. (Mama stands in front of the banner with her ladle. The Honourable's photographer takes the picture anyway. It's the best one.)

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Evening. Iyana-Wahala throws you a send-forth. Nobody organised it. Garba brings tea, Ada brings her speaker, Mama Put brings rice, and somehow there are fourteen chairs and forty people.

beats.speaker: ada
beats.text: Scholar! Before you go and forget us for Royal Crest people, dance! If you lose to me you must send me fabric from the Island.

won.toast: The street goes wild. Garba gives you a free tea for life. (Conditions apply.)

lost.toast: Ada wins. Mama laughs so hard she has to sit down.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: After midnight. Everybody has gone. Mama is washing pots and humming. She stops.

beats.speaker: mamaSomto
beats.text: Somto. At that school, people will ask who your father is. Who your mother is. What you have. (She dries her hands.) What will you say?

options.text: "Whatever keeps me there, Mama. I'll tell you the truth. Them, I don't know yet."

beats.title: Send-Forth
beats.summary: A morning frying, a photograph that will follow you, a street that danced for you. Tomorrow: Royal Crest.
